Research algebraic methods for establishing a Jónsson-Tarski-style representation theorem for the bimodal logic TM with primitives Since (S), Until (U), and Box (□), plus material implication (→) and bottom (⊥) as the primitive Boolean operators. The goal is to determine whether the Lindenbaum-Tarski algebra of TM forms a variety of Boolean algebras with operators (BAOs) that admits a concrete representation into complex algebras of relational structures (task frames). Key questions: (1) Since S and U are binary normal operators, does the standard Jónsson-Tarski representation for n-ary BAOs apply directly, or does the interaction with the S5 modal operator □ introduce complications? (2) What role does orthodox axiomatizability (no IRR rule) play — per Venema 1993 (Anti-Axioms), orthodox systems ensure closure under ultraproducts, but TM uses the IRR rule in the ConservativeExtension module; does this affect the algebraic representation? (3) Can the existing TenseS5Algebra.lean structure be extended to a full BAO with S/U operators, and does the Lindenbaum quotient construction yield a representable algebra? (4) What is the relationship between the parametric representation theorem (ParametricRepresentation.lean) and a Jónsson-Tarski-style algebraic representation — are they equivalent, or does one subsume the other? (5) How do the Prior-UZ/SZ axioms (discrete well-ordering) and the uniformity axioms (ordered abelian group structure) interact with the algebraic representation? Literature base: Venema 1991 (dissertation Ch2 + App A), Venema 1993 (Anti-Axioms), Goldblatt-Hodkinson-Venema 2003, Venema 1997 (Atom Structures), de Rijke-Venema 1995 (Sahlqvist for BAOs), Blackburn-de Rijke-Venema 2001 Ch5 (not yet obtained). All papers are in literature/ with markdown conversions.

active_projects.description: Redesign the FMP filtration for strict temporal semantics. The 2 sorry theorems in Decidability/FMP/TruthPreservation.lean — mcs_all_future_closure (line 263) and mcs_all_past_closure (line 281) — are deprecated because the temporal T-axiom (Gphi -> phi) is NOT valid under strict semantics. filtration_all_future_forward and filtration_all_past_forward depend on them. The FMP module is separate from the main decidability pipeline (decide is sorry-free), but completing it formally proves the finite model property. active_projects.description: Add time addition operator (+) to the bimodal logic TM. φ + ψ is true at (τ, x) iff ∃ y,z with x = y+z, φ true at (τ,y), ψ true at (τ,z). This internalizes the AddCommGroup structure of D into the object language, extending expressive power from FO[<] to FO[<,+] (Presburger arithmetic). Related to arrow logic (Venema), relevant logic (Routley-Meyer ternary frames), and separation logic (BI). Phase 1: add tadd/tsub constructors to Formula, truth clause in semantics. Phase 2: basic axioms (associativity, commutativity, identity, inverse). Phase 3: soundness proofs. Phase 4: interaction with G/H/U/S/□. Completeness (ternary canonical model) and decidability are open research problems — defer to later phases.

Add topological open set (interior) operator for dense and continuous temporal frames. On discrete ℤ the interior is trivial (discrete topology), but on dense ℚ and continuous ℝ it captures neighborhood-stable truth: Int(φ) true at t iff φ holds in an open neighborhood of t. Related to Dynamic Topological Logic (Kremer-Mints 2005), McKinsey-Tarski topological semantics for S4, and Fernandez-Duque intuitionistic temporal logic. Phase 1: add TopologicalSpace instance to TaskFrame for dense/continuous cases. Phase 2: add interior constructor to Formula with truth clause. Phase 3: axioms (S4-like: Int(φ)→φ, Int(φ)→Int(Int(φ))). Phase 4: interaction with temporal operators and S5 □. Note: DTL is not finitely axiomatizable (Fernandez-Duque 2014) — completeness may require non-standard techniques.

Develop a weak/reflexive temporal sub-language for discrete frames where G_w evaluates over the reflexive closure (y >= x) rather than the strict order (y > x). Prove completeness for this sub-language using standard Henkin canonical model methods (no chronicle construction, no IR rule), then transfer completeness to the strict system via model-theoretic argument, bypassing the succ_cofinal gap entirely.

Phase 1: Weak sub-language definition (~100 lines). G_w(phi) := phi AND G(phi), H_w := phi AND H(phi), F_w := phi OR F(phi), P_w := phi OR P(phi). Weak Until/Since with reflexive endpoints.

Phase 2: Weak axiom system (~200 lines). Derive weak axioms in the strict system. G_w(phi)->phi is trivial. Weak Z1 (FG_w(phi)->G_w(phi)) derivable from strict Z1.

Phase 3: Weak Henkin canonical model (~500-800 lines). Standard construction where each point is a distinct MCS. No chronicle, no IR rule, no gap scenario. Constant-MCS structurally impossible.

Phase 4: Z1 + IsSuccArchimedean in the weak model (~200-400 lines). Doets maximum principle (Claim 10) + compression from sum-of-zeta to single zeta (Claims 9-11).

Phase 5: Model-theoretic completeness transfer (~100 lines). IMPORTANT: Expressing strict G in terms of weak operators is impossible (U_w(phi,bot) = phi in weak semantics, so Next is not definable). Instead use model-theoretic argument: if psi is not provable in the strict system, then neg-psi is consistent in the strict system. Since every weak axiom is a strict theorem (G_w = phi AND G), neg-psi is consistent in the weak system. By weak completeness, there exists a weak countermodel. This is also a strict countermodel (same domain, same valuation, reinterpret <= as <). Contrapositive: valid under strict -> provable.

Phase 6: Integration (~100 lines). Wire weak completeness + transfer into existing pipeline.

Phase 7: Close the sorry (~50 lines). Replace the admitted limitDomSubtype_isSuccArchimedean in ChronicleToCountermodel.lean with the Henkin-derived IsSuccArchimedean, making dd_countermodel_chronicle_discrete sorry-free.
